sensors.name: left light sensor LLIGHT (light from above)

control_flow: driveInTheDark: if LLIGHT is below 30 %, drive forward at 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Drive along the line through the tunnel and out the other side.

decision_points.condition: the left light sensor reads below 30 %

branches.reason: The dimmest a tunnel gets is 40 %, so LLIGHT never reads below 30 % in the simulator.
branches.outcome: light below 30 %: it drives forward at 30 %
light 30 % or more: it goes on to stopAtWall
an obstacle is ahead: it stops
no obstacle ahead: it goes on to followLine

input_dimensions.dimension: whether there is a line through the tunnel
what is ahead on the line in the tunnel

scenarios.coded_response: It goes to stopAtWall, sees no obstacle, and follows the line: curve left on black, curve right on the floor
scenarios.initial_condition: On a line that runs through a tunnel, with light above 30 % and nothing in front of it
scenarios.trigger: The line tracker sees black, then the floor, again and again, until the line leaves the tunnel
scenarios.title: Follows the line through the tunnel
assumptions: The line runs through the tunnel and ends after its exit.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line through the tunnel and out to its end

scenarios.coded_response: It stops while the wall is ahead

assumptions: You didn't say it, but the stop-at-wall part of your program is meant to stop before walls.

The program follows a line to get anywhere: on a plain floor it curves in a circle, so without a line through the tunnel it circles instead of getting through.
